title: Incredibly effective
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 7, 2026
review: hese yellow sticky gnat traps work incredibly well! I honestly had no idea how many gnats were living throughout my indoor houseplants until I started using these. The traps filled up fast and made a huge difference almost immediately. I’m already on my second round because they’ve been so effective at catching them. Super easy to use, affordable, and oddly satisfying to see how many they trap. Highly recommend for anyone battling fungus gnats in houseplants!

title: Great for getting rid of the gnats
date: Reviewed in the United States on March 30, 2026
review: I love having my tropical plants indoors during the winter, but the gnats, aphids and other pests can be a big problem, especially when the plants are near the kitchen. These traps do a great job in capturing most of the flying pests. It's just a bit tricky not getting your fingers sticky when placing the traps on the included sticks.

title: Annoying dirt flies, get GONE!
date: Reviewed in the United States on December 1, 2025
review: Finding yourself with those annoying little dirt flies?  Not sure what they are called, but nothing I call them is appropriate for this review.  Talk about pesky the flies, not the product!  These things work great.  I'm not sure they will eliminate the problem but there is something satisfying (as bad as that sounds)  about seeing all the annoying flies that won't be flying around you on a little yellow sticky scoreboard.  I don't know if I eradicated colony as I moved and sold most of my house plants, and likely plant zero,  after getting the flies down to a noticable minimum evidenced by the reduction in annoying gnats in my orbit and the yellow score cards I changed out showing less confirmed kills.  Fast forward and I get some dirt from the local nursery for a new plant and bingo, more little flies.  I bought another kind of these, not this one, and they are way too big for my plants.  In hindsight, I should have bought these again.  Drawbacks on these, they are a pain to set up (imagine sticking to fingers and the loops coming out of the holder over and over to end up just sticking out straight -- which will still work, but not as well as intended).  With that said, these can easily be nested within your plant to catch the annoying gnats before they leave the pot for your personal space.  So, after trying this and another brand, I'd go with these again.

title: Great product!
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 12, 2026
review: These truly do work for fungus gnats i did have to double stack the yellow sticks for larger plants. It will not keep your plant from having fungus gnats, but it helps catch the ones that are in the air.

title: Definitely Work!
date: Reviewed in the United States on May 7, 2026
review: So I had a bunch of annoying gnats flying around me, plants and lying water. I placed these traps in my plants and they have definitely captured a lot of these bugs. It’s been about 3-weeks. They are now very random than the constant annoyance. I would recommend this item.

title: Put the traps in a jar next to the plant and not in the soil.
date: Reviewed in the United States on April 12, 2026
review: As I have stated in my first review, I am disappointed with the design feature of this product. The green stakes do not securely hold the yellow insect stickie traps which “snap open” and stick to delicate leaves or get covered in dirt.Solution: build the trap trees, but plant them in narrow glasses and place near the plants.They can be easily moved around and cause less functional problem.The product still seems expensive so I only give them three stars.

title: Love them
date: Reviewed in the United States on August 11, 2024
review: It’s small, amazing bug catcher it definitely does its job. I love that they come with sticks so you’re able to push them down in the dirt.  These ones are very easy to put together, I like that you can either use one or you can add two stickers to a stick. I would recommend buying these for your plants and the price is cheap.So I ordered a different brand that looks like a butterfly with a triangle shape bottom. Those were difficult to push down in the dirt and hard to kept them straight. I did take a picture of the other brand that is shaped like a butterfly to show what I was talking about.

title: Great job
date: Reviewed in the United States on August 20, 2024
review: I bought 17 new indoor hanging plants on line for my new home. I am sure each plant came with1,000 fungus gnats each. When you walked by them or disturbed them in any way you could see them crawling inside my white planters and then they start flying up your nose or in your eyes. I bought those yellow sticky flowers, birds etc. but they were huge, bulky and ugly. Saw these on the sticks&tried them, not as sticky,but how sticky do they have to be to trap those tiny pests?I love this product, It's just as effective, easier to use, and much less intrusive. They also don't stick out like a sore thumb & takes up much less room in the pots and can be hidden in the plant which is, after all why you bought the plants in the first place. I think this product is exactly what is needed to protect your beautiful plants.by the way if you have used those other HUGE stickers and then replaced them with these stake ones you'll probably see less bugs on them only because you have already caught some with the other larger ones first,again I love this product and won't go back to those tiger (kitty cat style) ones, sorry just an exaggeration about the difference in the size.
